transcript: Header: 2025-09-02 10:00 PDT | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luis Martinez (Redwood Eng); Sara Gupta (Nimbus CTO), Tom Reynolds (ML Eng), Maya Patel (Data Eng)
00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the hour. quick agenda: recap last week's INT8 baseline, go through the FP8 runs priya kicked off, and decide next steps for the pilot
00:12 Sara: sounds good, we have 60 minutes. main thing for us is quality impact — if we can get near-parity with int8 or fp8 at lower cost, we move to a 2-week pilot on dedicated nodes
00:26 Alex: perfect. priya, can you walk through the FP8 numbers? i saw the spreadsheet but some cells were cryptic

00:33 Priya: yeah so quick caveat — the FP8 run was still on the same micro-batching config as INT8, we used the 512 token step size for the perf runs. initial results: FP8 gives ~1.6x token throughput vs FP16, INT8 gives ~1.9x on the p4d-ish instance we emulated
00:49 Tom: emulated? are you running on cloud instances or dedicated hardware for these numbers? recall we told you our infra is on-prem-ish with A100 80GB nodes

00:58 Priya: right — these were on Redwood dedicated staging on AWS g5-like hardware to be comparable. we did a quick on-prem spot-check with your sample and numbers were directionally similar but we'll need your exact config to be precise
01:12 Maya: there were a few inference errors we noticed with INT8 on longer prompts — more hallucinations in the clinical note generation tests
01:21 Luis: yep i saw that in the rouge numbers; the average rouge drop was about 2.3 points for INT8 on the long-doc split, FP8 was closer at 0.8 drop. but variance is high on outlier prompts
01:37 Sara: can you quantify "outlier" — is this >5% of prompts or like 0.5%? we care about tail correctness for regulatory reasons

01:45 Priya: good question. for our sample, about 4-6% of prompts had >5% divergence on the KL metric. most of those were very long context chains with many system messages and nested bullet lists — could be kv-cache alignment issues
02:02 Tom: kv-cache — are you saying the cache retrieval/prefix isn't matching after quantization? that's a concern, we use prefix caching heavily in prod to reduce token spend

02:11 Priya: what we saw is subtle: FP8 preserves the kv values more consistently than INT8 at extreme lengths. INT8 compression/quant step introduces tiny bias that accumulates across many tokens, affecting conditional outputs. not catastrophic but shows up in clinical extraction tasks
02:28 Alex: OK so practical implication: INT8 is cheapest but higher risk on long prompts; FP8 is middle ground. we should map this to Nimbus's tolerance for tail errors. sara, what's acceptable?

02:37 Sara: for automated summary we need >95% alignment to human-curated labels; for downstream extraction (PII masking) we need near 99% precision. small drop is ok in summaries but not in extraction

02:50 Luis: from an infra standpoint FP8 also had slightly higher memory use than INT8 but lower than FP16 — it's a tradeoff with throughput. our kernel selection heuristics in the runtime can pick different GEMM kernels which changed perf by ~10% between runs
03:06 Tom: were these runs using continuous batching and prefix caching? or cold-start per request?
03:12 Priya: runs used Redwood's default continuous batching (2-4ms batch window) and prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes. we also ran a cold-start subset to show worst-case latencies
03:25 Maya: can you share latency percentiles? p95/p99 are what our SLOs care about

03:31 Priya: sure — for INT8 p95 was 190ms, p99 320ms on 4k context; FP8 p95 220ms, p99 350ms; FP16 p95 380ms, p99 680ms. those are tokens/sec converted to single-response latency with our batching knobs
03:50 Tom: so INT8 is fastest, but we saw quality drops. is the quality delta tunable by calibration or mixed-precision?

03:58 Priya: yes, two levers: mixed-precision pipelines (kv-cache in FP16 + head in INT8) and per-layer quantization thresholds. we tried layer-wise hybrid quant and that recovers ~60% of the rouge drop on the long-doc split at the cost of some throughput — ~1.2x vs FP16 baseline
04:20 Alex: that sounds promising. could you outline the suggested config for Nimbus if they want to prioritize extraction precision?

04:27 Priya: recommendation would be: use FP8 for main inference, enable KV cache in FP16 (store keys/values in FP16) for long contexts, and keep final softmax/head in FP16 for extraction tasks. optionally enable mixed layer quant for the last 6 transformer blocks
04:44 Sara: that seems reasonable. we have compliance concerns about any approach that increases nondeterminism — do you have audit logs that can tie back outputs to model variant and quant config?

04:55 Alex: yes we do — Redwood Console logs model version, quant profile, node id, and random seeds where relevant. we can surface a per-request fingerprint for audits. we'll attach the security docs asap
05:06 Maya: please include retention and KMS usage — our security team will check that against ISO/SOC2 certs
05:14 Alex: noted, i'll include SOC2 scope and KMS details in the packet. priya, quick show of the spreadsheet?
05:22 Priya: sharing the bench sheet link in chat — looks like: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/nimbus-quant-2025-09-02.xlsx (internal preview). main tabs: perf, quality, long-doc-outliers
05:33 Tom: got it. i see cells flagged with TODOs — there are some missing columns for your KL metric, can you compute aggregated KL per prompt group?
05:41 Priya: yes i'll add aggregate columns. also we'll add a per-prompt trace for top 50 outliers so you can inspect exact token drift

05:52 Luis: on the ops side we should discuss memory pinning and NUMA placement for your on-prem A100; FP8 had different page-fault patterns in our sim. if you want dedicated nodes we can preconfigure the runtime to avoid those cliffs
06:06 Tom: we'd like that — our infra team will want a runbook for node tuning, and a plan to failover to hosted if dedicated capacity is saturated

06:16 Alex: Redwood supports smart routing — can route by policy (latency/cost/region) and automatic fallback to hosted or a more conservative quant profile if errors spike. we can add a canary to flip profiles automatically
06:29 Sara: that fallback is critical for us. what's the ops overhead to set that up?

06:34 Priya: setup is mostly config + one-off tests. we typically do a canary rollout on 5% traffic for a day and monitor quality/regressions; SE team handles initial config and we'll hand over runbook to your SREs
06:48 Maya: about interpretability — do you collect token-level logits so we can reproduce why a token changed? that's part of our review process
06:55 Priya: we do collect optional token logits and attention weights on debug traces; it's off by default for privacy/cost but can be enabled for short windows during debug runs
07:08 Tom: cost question: how much cheaper would an INT8 deployment be on Dedicated vs FP8? ballpark numbers are fine
07:14 Alex: rough ballpark from our testbed: INT8 dedicated runtime is ~35-45% lower cost per token vs FP16; FP8 is ~20-30% lower. exact numbers depend on batching and your request distribution
07:28 Sara: hmm that's meaningful. but if extraction fails we're exposed. is mixed precision a good compromise?
07:34 Priya: yes, mixed gives most of the cost benefit while protecting tail quality. we can instrument hybrid configs and run a short AB test on some production traffic in a safe environment

07:46 Luis: from reliability side we also recommend enabling per-route fallback to FP16 for requests flagged as high-risk (e.g., labeled pii extraction). that way the majority runs on FP8 but flagged ones use safer profile
07:59 Maya: good idea. we will provide a rule file for flagged routes — mostly PII and regulatory templates
08:06 Alex: next, let's align on deliverables and timeline — priya, summary of what you'll do this week?

08:12 Priya: deliverables: (1) full INT8 & FP8 quality sweep on 4k context with per-prompt breakdown, (2) mixed-precision configs and perf tradeoffs, (3) updated bench spreadsheet and per-prompt traces. ETA 2025-09-09
08:28 Tom: we'll send the eval set and prompt distribution tonight — look for an email with a GCS link
08:34 Sara: also include acceptance criteria: if mixed config keeps extraction precision >=99% and summary rouge within 1 point vs FP16 we can proceed to pilot
08:44 Alex: got it, we'll codify that acceptance criteria in the pilot doc. one more ops question — if we move to Dedicated, how long to provision nodes?
08:52 Priya: standard lead time is 2-3 weeks for reserved capacity, we can do express provisioning for initial pilot in 3-5 days depending on region and hardware
09:02 Maya: any compliance blocker for logs and KMS?
09:06 Alex: no blockers we've seen; we just need to sign the DPA and provide KMS integration docs. I'll include the SOC2/ISO excerpts in the packet
09:17 Tom: on the technical deep-dive if FP8 still has variance we'll need a session on quantization-aware activation scaling and calibration. can the SE team run that?
09:26 Priya: yes happy to lead a 60-90m deep-dive; propose week of 2025-09-15, we'll bring the model owner and runtime engineer
09:36 Sara: ok book that tentatively and we'll confirm after we see the next run
09:42 Alex: perfect. any other open questions?
09:46 Maya: one small ask — can you include a simple cost calculator mapping our qps distribution to monthly spend per quant profile?
09:52 Alex: yes i'll include a cost calc and a sample SLA + fallback config. will send along with pricing

09:58 Priya: closing note — two quick risks: (1) outlier prompt drift for INT8 and (2) slight NUMA/pinning issues on FP8 we observed in our sim. we can mitigate both with the mixed config and node tuning

10:12 Alex: great summary. recap of next steps: priya runs the full sweep and updates sheet by 9/9; alex sends pricing + security packet by 9/5; tom sends eval set by 9/4; schedule quant deep-dive week of 9/15. i'll follow up in email with links
10:25 Sara: thanks everyone, appreciate the thoroughness. talk soon
10:30 End of recording
